story.iWant: a unified LLM client with provider selection and fallback
story.soThat: Annie can use multiple LLM providers reliably

tasks.task: Implement LLM Client base class with provider configuration from environment variables
Implement provider failover logic with 2-second timeout
Implement error handling for both providers failing with structured logging
Implement rate limiting and retry logic
Implement basic chat completion method with OpenAI-compatible format
Update LLM health check in main.py
End-to-end testing of all LLM client features

acceptanceCriteria.ac: Given Grok-4 API key is configured, when I initialize the LLM client, then it authenticates and can make API calls successfully
Given the LLM client, when I configure providers, then it supports Grok-4 (primary) and ChatGPT-5 (fallback) with provider selection logic
Given Grok-4 fails (network error, API error, rate limit), when I call the LLM client, then it automatically falls back to ChatGPT-5 within 2 seconds
Given both LLMs fail, when I call the LLM client, then it returns a clear, user-friendly error message: "I'm experiencing technical difficulties. Please try again in a moment."
Given the LLM client, when I check error handling, then provider failures are logged with error details, retry attempts, and fallback actions
Given the LLM client, when rate limiting occurs, then it handles rate limit errors gracefully and suggests retry after appropriate delay
Given the LLM client, when I check configuration, then API keys, base URLs, and timeouts are configurable via environment variables

package.name: httpx
package.note: Already added for async HTTP calls

constraints.constraint: Use OpenAI-compatible API format for both Grok-4 and ChatGPT-5 endpoints
Provider failover must complete within 2 seconds (p95 performance requirement)
Use httpx.AsyncClient for async HTTP calls with configurable timeout
Follow structured logging pattern: get_logger(__name__) with masked API keys
Use existing config.get_config() for environment variable access
Error messages must be user-friendly, not expose internal details
All API keys must be configurable via environment variables
Rate limit detection via HTTP 429 status code and retry-after header parsing

interface.name: LLMClient.health_check
interface.description: Check primary provider availability, return "ok", "degraded", or "unavailable"

tests.standards: Use pytest framework with asyncio support for async methods. Mock external LLM API calls using unittest.mock.AsyncMock and @patch decorator. Follow test pyramid: 60% unit tests (fast, isolated), 30% integration tests (with test API keys), 10% E2E tests. Target 80%+ code coverage. Tests should be behavior-focused, maintainable, and fast (unit tests < 1s each). Use pytest fixtures for common setup.

ideas.idea: Test Grok-4 authentication with valid API key, verify successful initialization
Test provider selection logic (Grok-4 vs ChatGPT-5) based on LLM_PROVIDER config
Test automatic failover: mock Grok-4 failure, verify switch to ChatGPT-5 within 2s timeout
Test failover with different error types: network errors, API errors, timeouts, rate limits
Test both providers failing: verify user-friendly error message returned
Test error logging: verify provider failures logged with structured extra fields
Test rate limit handling: mock HTTP 429 response, verify retry-after header parsing
Test configuration via environment variables: GROK_API_KEY, CHATGPT_API_KEY, LLM_PROVIDER
Test chat_completion method with both providers using mocked responses
Test health_check method returns "ok", "degraded", or "unavailable" based on provider state
